triangles_per_figure.accessories_lod1_extra: accessory mesh (cartbox, canteen, haversack, sash, scabbard, sword, cavalry set) adds up to about 330 triangles to a mid figure; included in the lod1 median below

slopes_gpu_ms_per_Mtri.note: least-squares fit of the GPU pass sum against tris_M over each prototype scaling suite (Measured runs, Computed slope); the near slope for this module's LOD0 is interpolated in triangles per figure between the q1/q2/q3 suites

screen_space_error_lod.rule: a figure of projected height h px needs 0.09 h^2 triangles (PLAN section 3.4); h = 1683 / d at 1080p, 60 degree vertical field of view

measured_handover.method: MEASURED with the software rasteriser (flat colours, one key light), 1080p 60 degree FOV, 6 men x 2 views; NOT a measurement of the product shader
measured_handover.rule: radius rule (1080p; the distances scale with vertical resolution, since a pixel covers 1.069 mm per metre of distance at 1080p): LOD0 for d < 10 m, LOD1 for 10 <= d < 13 m, LOD2 for 13 <= d < 55 m, impostor beyond; each swap is a 15 percent dithered cross-fade centred on the distance with 10 percent hysteresis. LOD1 is the narrow bridge off the 45,000-triangle mesh: LOD2 (about 568 triangles) already matches LOD1 within the gates from 13 m; where the governor has pulled the radii in, the LOD1 band widens.
caveats: the impostor swap meets the 0.5 px silhouette gate only from 55 m with the 48 x 64 atlas (texel 31 mm); a 96 x 128 atlas would meet it from about half that distance at 4 times the bytes (about 20 MB BC7)
the impostor mean L* step is 1.5 to 3.5 in the rasteriser test beyond 40 m (above the 2 L* gate at 55 to 100 m): per-class brightness normalisation of the baked shade is OPEN (EG-FIG-0011)
LOD1 meshes are silhouette-class representatives; the measured numbers include the representative-versus-actual mismatch (hats, weapons, trousers)

fits_125k.question: do 125,000 figures still fit the 7 ms allowance for characters on WebGPU (Arc iGPU, 1080p) with 45,000-triangle LOD0?
fits_125k.answer: YES for the seven prototype shots rescaled to the measured radii (see per_shot_with_the_radius_rule; the smoke-dominated line shot misses 16.7 ms as it already did unscaled); NO for the worst case, a dense formation (1.8 men per square metre) filling the whole view from 3 m: 12.0 ms of figure cost (including the far pass) against 7 ms. There the budgeted nearest-first rule keeps LOD0 to 61 figures and the adaptive bias moves the rest; G4 is then not met (stated)

bias_to_fit_dense_view.meaning: the largest b (every hand-over distance multiplied by b) at which the DENSE worst-case view fits the 7 ms allowance: the radius rule WebGL2 must follow in that view (WebGL2: LOD0 radius (b x 10 m), and so on); the far pass alone is 1.80 ms (WebGPU) and 3.07 ms (WebGL2, scaled 1.7), so below b about the value where the far pass fills the allowance no radius can fit and the resolution scale is the next lever

fits_125k.shot_scaling_assumption: MODELLED: the prototype shots (near radius 40 m, mid radius 300 m) are rescaled by the area ratios (R / 40)^2 and (R / 300)^2, i.e. uniform density; real formations are denser along the line, so the true LOD0 counts are higher in the shots that look along a line

webgl2_distance_rule.distance_rule: WebGL2 (near slope 4.52 ms per Mtri, mid 3.125: about 4.2 times the WebGPU near cost): the LOD0 disc is chosen by a triangle BUDGET, not a fixed radius: B0 = (7 ms - mid and far cost) / 4.52 ms per Mtri = about 0.00 M triangles = 0 LOD0 figures in the DENSE view (the mid and far cost alone exceed 7 ms there: the dense-view rule is the bias b = 0.39 on every distance); in the thin views of the prototype shots the budget is the formula above. LOD0 goes to the nearest figures until the budget is spent (a radius of 3.0 m in a dense formation, up to 10 m in a thin one); the rest take LOD1 and LOD2 at the same radii as WebGPU, and where the budget is short the adaptive bias below applies.
webgl2_distance_rule.near_mesh_cap_alternative: a hard LOD0 of about 5,000 triangles on WebGL2 (the prototype note) is NOT adopted: LOD0 stays one mesh and its radius shrinks instead

adaptive_lod_bias.name: adaptive LOD-bias controller (spec; implemented by the renderer, not here)
adaptive_lod_bias.variable: b in [0.25, 1]: every hand-over distance d_i is used as b * d_i (b = 1 is the measured gate distance)
adaptive_lod_bias.input: GPU time of the character passes (timestamp query) minus the fixed passes, smoothed over 8 frames; CPU fallback: the previous frame time
adaptive_lod_bias.target: 7 ms of the 16.7 ms (PLAN section 3.4), on WebGL2 as well
adaptive_lod_bias.law: e = (t_fig - 7) / 7; b <- clamp(b - 0.35 e - 0.05 * integral(e), 0.25, 1); change per frame limited to 2 percent; dead band +-5 percent; recovery (b rising) limited to 0.5 percent per frame so the picture does not breathe
adaptive_lod_bias.order_of_reduction: the LOD0 radius is multiplied by b first (45,000 triangles per figure), the LOD1/LOD2 swap by sqrt(b), the impostor swap by b^(1/3); the resolution scale is the next lever (PLAN G1 path 5); the figure COUNT and the content are never reduced
adaptive_lod_bias.budgeted_selection: instead of a pure radius, the nearest-first triangle budget: a GPU histogram of figure distances in 1 m bins (one atomic per figure) gives the cumulative LOD0 triangle count; the LOD0 radius is the distance where it reaches B0 = (7 ms - rest) / slope

bytes.bone_matrix_clips: ANIMATION owns this: 600 clips x 180 frames x 60 bones x 3 texels x 8 B = 156 MB (PLAN G15); the mid skeleton has 36 bones: 94 MB

draw_calls.near: near figures draw their parts instanced by part id: at most one draw per distinct part id in the near list; the near list is at most 1,536 figures, a typical dense unit uses 60-120 distinct ids (24 heads + hair + coats + trousers + hats + arms); WebGPU multi-draw-indirect reduces these to 2-3 submissions
draw_calls.mid: one instanced draw per silhouette class present in the mid radius (351 classes exist in the kit-wide sample; the PLAN shots saw 2,000-4,800 mid figures from a few dozen units: expect 20-80 classes) plus one per accessory class (22)
draw_calls.far: 1 instanced quad draw for all impostor classes (atlas indexed by class) and the sub-7-px dab pass
draw_calls.frame_total_estimate: 100-250 draw calls on WebGL2, under 10 submissions with multi-draw-indirect on WebGPU (Modelled)

mobile.status: MODELLED: no mobile GPU was measured (the PLAN lists mobile GPUs as not measured); the factors below are the largest slowdown against the Arc Pro 140T iGPU that the model tolerates, not predictions of any phone
mobile.model: figure_ms(device) = figure_ms(Arc) x slowdown; budget = the 7 ms the PLAN leaves for characters at 60 fps (section 3.4)

fixed_radius_lod_prototype_radii.note: LOD radii of the prototype (near 40 m, mid 300 m) with these meshes: the design the PLAN replaces

screen_space_error_lod.note: the PLAN rule (section 3.4): geometry is resolution-bound; this is the shipped LOD policy

levers: frame-time governor moves the LOD distances and the resolution scale, never the content or the figure count (PLAN G1 path 5)
LOD0 radius 0 removes the near cost entirely (all figures use LOD1/LOD2/impostor)
impostor-only beyond 13 m cuts the mid list to the 5-13 m band
mobile.lod_budget_rule: no figure count is capped: all 125,000 figures draw every frame (impostors); only the distance at which a richer mesh is used moves

g1_gate.target: 60 fps with p99 <= 16.7 ms at 1080p on the iGPU, 4K on the dGPU; CPU <= 8 ms at 4x throttle
g1_gate.figure_budget_ms: the PLAN leaves about 7 ms of the 16.7 ms for characters on the Arc iGPU (section 3.4)
g1_gate.status: ON PAPER ONLY: verification list item 1 measures it

limits: the near/mid counts are the prototype's (165,000-soldier world); with 125,000 figures they are an upper bound
vertex skinning cost for the 60-bone near list is the prototype's measured CPU pose + FK (1.84 us per figure) and is not changed by the meshes
the prototype's per-figure pass (shadow casters) is included in the slope because the slope is fitted to the pass sum
